cards.text: A long time after the LORD gave Israel rest from all their enemies, Joshua, Israel's leader, is old and well along in years. He calls in all Israel, including the elders, leaders, judges and officers. Friend, when the boss pulls EVERY department into one room, nobody is checking their phone.

cards.question: Joshua tells them they've seen everything the LORD did to these nations for their sake. He says it was the LORD their God who ___ for them.

cards.text: Joshua says he has already given the tribes their land, from the Jordan west to the Great Sea, and that includes the nations still living there. Handing out land that still has people in it? Now THAT is confidence.

cards.question: About the nations still in the land, Joshua says the LORD their God will ___ them out, so Israel can ___ their land.

cards.text: Now Joshua gets to his charge, and he tells the whole room to be very strong. He says it like a personal trainer at six in the morning, and I'm the guy in the back still tying his apron.

cards.question: Joshua tells Israel to be very strong. Strong enough to do what?

answers.text: Keep all that's written in the Law of Moses
Drive out every nation all by themselves
Build a great temple for the LORD

cards.question: Joshua says it's okay for Israel to turn aside from the Book of the Law a little, as long as they keep most of it.

cards.text: Now about those nations still living among them. Joshua says not to associate with them. No hanging out, no group chat, NOTHING.

cards.question: Joshua says Israel can bow down to the gods of those nations, as long as they don't serve them.
Instead of the gods of those nations, who does Joshua tell Israel to hold fast to, as they've done to this day?

cards.text: Joshua points back at the record: the LORD has driven out great and powerful nations before Israel, and to this day no one can stand against them. Me? I lost an argument to the dead batteries I shared that drawer with, and they had NO charge.

cards.question: Joshua says one Israelite can put a thousand enemies to flight. How is that possible?

answers.text: The LORD their God fights for them
Their enemies have no weapons left
Their soldiers were trained by Moses

cards.question: So Joshua tells Israel to watch themselves carefully. What does he want them watching for?

answers.text: That they love the LORD their God
That their borders stay well guarded
That their armies stay ready to fight

cards.text: Then Joshua flips it around. What if they turn away, cling to the nations still among them, and intermarry and associate with them? I bet that room got real quiet.

cards.question: Joshua says that if Israel clings to those nations, the LORD will keep driving those nations out anyway.
Joshua warns that if Israel clings to those nations, those nations will become something for Israel until Israel perishes from this good land. What will they become?

cards.text: Then Joshua says, "Now behold, today I am going the way of all the earth," and he reminds them of something they know with all their heart and soul.

cards.question: Joshua says some of the good promises the LORD made to Israel have failed along the way.

cards.text: Not one promise failed. Everything was fulfilled. Friend, I promised myself ONE cookie today, and I'm on cookie number nine.

cards.question: But Joshua says it works both ways. Just as every ___ thing the LORD promised came to pass, the LORD will also bring the ___ He threatened.
Joshua says the anger of the LORD would burn against Israel. What would bring that on?

answers.text: Breaking His covenant and serving other gods
Losing a battle to the nations around them
Leaving the land to go live somewhere else

cards.text: Go that way, Joshua says, and they will quickly perish from this good land the LORD gave them. An old man with one last thing to say doesn't waste a single word.

findings.problem: The question frames this as a warning and says these nations will be this 'until Israel perishes from this good land.' Card 5 has already shown the outcome is bad. Both wrong answers are positive ('A wall of protection', 'A source of riches'), so the setup rules them out and only the right answer fits.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The second blank sits right before 'He threatened,' and the question opens with 'it works both ways.' That rules out the wrong answers 'reward' and 'peace,' since nobody threatens a reward or peace. 'calamity' is the only word that fits.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The storyteller line 'An old man with one last thing to say doesn't waste a single word' adds a fact: that this is Joshua's last speech. Joshua 24 has him gather Israel at Shechem and speak again, so Scripture shows the claim is not true.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can add a storyteller's line to carry the moment, like "But the Lord isn't finished with him," as long as it adds no facts.

findings.problem: The joke makes up a new event in the junk drawer: Papa Dorin losing an argument to the dead batteries. papa-dorin.md says he 'never adds anything new' to his backstory, but his jokes 'can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.' That allowance names the bakery, not the drawer. Yet the joke logic test's own example ('the dead batteries I shared that drawer with') suggests drawer callbacks are expected.
findings.question: May Papa Dorin's jokes make up small new moments set in the junk drawer, like losing an argument to the batteries? Or is the allowance for made-up moments limited to his bakery?
